title: Minimum Operations to Make Array Equal II
summary: Given two integer arrays nums1 and nums2 of the same length n, and an integer k, you can increment an element in nums1 by k and decrement another by k.
statement: Given two integer arrays nums1 and nums2 of the same length n, and an integer k, you can increment an element in nums1 by k and decrement another by k. Determine the least number of such operations needed to make nums1 equal to nums2, or return -1 if it's impossible.
constraints: One operation increases one nums1 element by k and decreases another nums1 element by k.
Return the minimum operations making nums1 equal nums2, or -1 if impossible.
When k is zero, only already-equal arrays can be transformed.
reference_solution:
def minimum_balanced_transfer_operations(nums1,nums2,k):
    if k==0:return 0 if nums1==nums2 else -1
    supplied=needed=0
    for first,second in zip(nums1,nums2):
        difference=first-second
        if difference%k:return -1
        if difference>0:supplied+=difference//k
        else:needed-=difference//k
    return supplied if supplied==needed else -1

hints: Each operation preserves the total sum and changes two positions by exact multiples of k.
Reject any non-divisible difference and separately total the surplus and deficit units.
If k is zero, compare the arrays directly; otherwise require the two unit totals to match.
Every operation pairs one surplus unit with one deficit unit, so their common total is both necessary and sufficient and is the minimum count.
